answer: Forging thousands of sybils means funding thousands of stakes plus compute for each sigil, so costs scale linearly while rewards stay fixed. Each agent must stake a quartz-bonded deposit and solve a unique per-epoch challenge tied to its registered identity, like carving a distinct juniper sigil only it can produce. A rotating lantern audit randomly spot-checks identities; failed checks burn the quartz stake, making mass fakery economically ruinous. From sa0028's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
